3.내가 마게도냐로 갈 때에 너를 권하여 에베소에 머물라 한 것은 어떤:
3.As I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine, neither give heed to fables and endless genealogies, which minister questions, rather than godly edifying which is in faith.
 - That's why he left Timothy there. To stop them from teaching other doctrines, to stop them from fussing over fables and endless genealogies. Things like Greek and Roman mythology. Look at the gods there, they marry their daughters, it's a total mess, right? The Greeks lived loosely, so they made up gods that looked like themselves, you see. These things only stir up arguments. Leaving Timothy there was to stop that kind of thing.
<딤전1:5> 이 교훈의 목적은 청결한 마음과 선한 양심과 거짓이 없는: <1 Tim 1:5> Now the end of the commandment is charity out of a pure heart, and of a good conscience, and of faith unfeigned:
사람들이 복음에서 벗어나 율법의 선생이 되려고들 하는데 자기가 무슨 말을: People stray from the gospel and want to be teachers of the law, but they don't even know what they're saying. The law isn't for the righteous, but for the lawless, the disobedient, the ungodly, sinners, the unholy, the profane, murderers of fathers and mothers, manslayers, whoremongers, sodomites (gays), menstealers, liars, perjured persons, and whoever goes against sound doctrine.
<딤전1:17~20> 만세의 왕 곧 썩지 아니하고 보이지 아니하고 홀로:
<1 Tim 1:17~20> Now unto the King eternal, immortal, invisible, the only God, be honour and glory for ever and ever. Amen. This charge I commit unto thee, son Timothy, according to the prophecies which went before on thee, that thou by them mightest war a good warfare; holding faith, and a good conscience; which some having put away concerning faith have made shipwreck: of whom is Hymenaeus and Alexander; whom I have delivered unto Satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
 - You must always be a good person, have a good conscience. But he says he has handed over to Satan the people who threw away this conscience. Hymenaeus shows up in 2 Tim 2:17 as one who says the resurrection is past already, and Alexander seems to be someone who gave testimony against Paul. The early church had fearsomely strict church discipline. If they said, "I hand you over to Satan in the name of the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit," you were as good as dead.
<딤전2:5> 하나님은 한 분이시요 또 하나님과 사람 사이에 중보도 한:
<1 Tim 2:5> For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus;
 - The Roman Catholic church keeps saying ‘Mary, the pope, the saints are mediators,’ but the mediator is only one, Jesus Christ.
<딤전2:9~15> 또 이와 같이 여자들도 아담한 옷을 입으며 염치와 정:
<1 Tim 2:9~15> In like manner also, that women adorn themselves in modest apparel, with shamefacedness and sobriety; not with broided hair, or gold, or pearls, or costly array; but (which becometh women professing godliness) with good works.
 - Don't dress yourself up with clothes or jewelry; dressing yourself up with good works is the best cosmetic there is.
<딤전2:11~12> 여자는 일절 순종함으로 조용히 배우라 여자의 가르치: <1 Tim 2:11~12> Let the woman learn in silence with all subjection. But I suffer not a woman to teach, nor to usurp authority over the man, but to be in silence.
이것은 창조의 원리를 이야기 하는 겁니다. <딤전2:13~15> 이는 아: This is talking about the principle of creation. <1 Tim 2:13~15> For Adam was first formed, then Eve. And Adam was not deceived, but the woman being deceived was in the transgression. Notwithstanding she shall be saved in childbearing, if they continue in faith and charity and holiness with sobriety.
해산함으로 구원을 받는다는게 무슨 말이예요? 칼빈은 이걸 ‘여성의 역할을: What does it mean to be saved through childbearing? Calvin interpreted this as ‘by fulfilling the woman's role...’ It speaks of bearing children as something so important it's compared to salvation. Especially our sisters here: when God made woman, He created her as a helper fit for the man, you know. To help someone, you have to be better than that person, right? Women have that ability. The ability to help someone and build them up. This is a truly important ability. Especially being able to bear and raise children is a tremendous thing. It's carrying history forward, and cultivating God's inheritance. So much so that doing this faithfully is said to lead to salvation.
3. 3장의 내용\n1) 감독의 자격:
3. Contents of chapter 3
1) Qualifications of a bishop
<딤전3:1> 미쁘다 이 말이여, 사람이 감독의 직분을 얻으려 하면 선한:
<1 Tim 3:1> This is a true saying, If a man desire the office of a bishop, he desireth a good work.
 - Wanting to be a bishop isn't about wielding some power; it's wanting to do good work
<딤전3:2~5> 그러므로 감독은 책망할 것이 없으며 한 아내의 남편이: <1 Tim 3:2~5> A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, vigilant, sober, of good behaviour, given to hospitality, apt to teach; not given to wine, no striker; but patient, not a brawler, not covetous; one that ruleth well his own house, having his children in subjection with all gravity; (for if a man know not how to rule his own house, how shall he take care of the church of God?)
<딤전3:6> 새로 입교한 자도 말지니 교만하여져서 마귀를 정죄하는 그:
<1 Tim 3:6> Not a novice, lest being lifted up with pride he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
 - No matter how well educated or capable someone is, you shouldn't make a person who just joined the church an elder
<딤전3:7> 또한 외인에게서도 선한 증거를 얻은 자라야 할지니 비방과:
<1 Tim 3:7> Moreover he must have a good report of them which are without; lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
 - A very important part. An elder shouldn't be someone recognized only inside the church; you should appoint someone already respected as an elder in the community, outside the church.
 2) Qualifications of a deacon
<딤전3:8~10> 이와 같이 집사들도 단정하고 일구 이언을 하지 아니하:
<1 Tim 3:8~10> Likewise must the deacons be grave, not doubletongued, not given to much wine, not greedy of filthy lucre; holding the mystery of the faith in a pure conscience. And let these also first be proved; then let them use the office of a deacon, being found blameless.
 - Even someone like this, appoint him only after he's been tested.
<딤전3:11~13> 여자들도 이와 같이 단정하고 참소하지 말며 절제하며: <1 Tim 3:11~13> Even so must the women be grave, not slanderers, sober, faithful in all things. Let the deacons be the husbands of one wife, ruling their children and their own houses well. For they that have used the office of a deacon well purchase to themselves a good degree, and great boldness in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
<딤전4:1~2> 그러나 성령이 밝히 말씀하시기를 후일에 어떤 사람들이:
<1 Tim 4:1~2> Now the Spirit speaketh expressly, that in the latter times some shall depart from the faith, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines of devils; speaking lies in hypocrisy; having their conscience seared with a hot iron;
 - Don't believe every spirit; discern, and know whether it's truly the Spirit of God or a spirit that makes a fool of the church.
<딤전4:3~13> 음식은 하나님이 지으신 것이다. 감사함으로 먹으면 문: <1 Tim 4:3~13> Food is something God made. If you eat it with thanksgiving, there's no problem. Bodily exercise profits a little. But godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise even of the life to come.
오직 말과 행실과 사랑과 믿음과 정절에 대하여 믿는 자에게 본이 되어 내: Be thou an example of the believers, in word, in conversation, in charity, in faith, in purity. Till I come, give attendance to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
<딤전5:1> 늙은이를 꾸짖지 말고 권하되 아비에게 하듯 하며 젊은이를: <1 Tim 5:1> Rebuke not an elder, but intreat him as a father; and the younger men as brethren;
<딤전5:2~3> 늙은 여자를 어미에게 하듯 하며 젊은 여자를 일절 깨끗: <1 Tim 5:2~3> The elder women as mothers; the younger as sisters, with all purity. Honour widows that are widows indeed.
<딤전5:4~8> 부모에게 보답하는 것을 배우게 하라.(효를 가르치라): <1 Tim 5:4~8> Let them learn to requite their parents. (Teach them to honor their parents)
You must take good care of your relatives, especially your family. Otherwise you're worse than an unbeliever.
<딤전5:17~18> 잘 다스리는 장로들을 배나 존경할 자로 알되 말씀과:
<1 Tim 5:17~18> Let the elders that rule well be counted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in the word and doctrine. For the scripture saith, Thou shalt not muzzle the ox that treadeth out the corn. And, The labourer is worthy of his reward.
 - In today's terms, respect the teaching elders, the pastors, and just as it says not to muzzle the ox, give them fitting pay.
<딤전5:23> 이제부터는 물만 마시지 말고 네 비위와 자주 나는 병을:
<1 Tim 5:23> Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach's sake and thine often infirmities.
 - It seems Timothy had stomach trouble, and even though wine was medicine for it, he never let it touch his lips. So Paul says, it's fine as medicine, try drinking a little. That's the level godliness ought to be at.
6. 6장의 내용\n - 아무리 같은 교회 안에 있어도 노예가 상전을‘오:
6. Contents of chapter 6
 - No matter if they're in the same church, a slave shouldn't go up to his master and say,‘Oh brother.’ He should serve him even better. It's not the servant calling his master brother; what's right is the master lifting the servant up and treating him as a brother.
 -Verse 8: pastor, church member, minister, whoever, the basic attitude of every believer is to be content if you have food and clothing.
<딤전6:9~10> 부하려 하는 자들은 시험과 올무와 여러 가지 어리석고:
<1 Tim 6:9~10> But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition. For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
 - You cannot serve God and money both. If I go beyond liking money to serving it? Then I'm not serving God. Serving money means giving money too much authority. Honestly, with money you can do almost anything, right? Even so, you try to solve everything with money, and that's exactly why you mustn't love money too much. Money is just a handy tool. You should think of it only that far, and not go any further.
<딤전6:17~21> 네가 이 세대에 부한 자들을 명하여 마음을 높이지: <1 Tim 6:17~21> Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy; that they do good, that they be rich in good works, ready to distribute, willing to communicate; laying up in store for themselves a good foundation against the time to come, that they may lay hold on true life. O Timothy, keep that which is committed to thy trust, avoiding profane and vain babblings, and oppositions of science falsely so called: which some professing have erred concerning the faith. Grace be with you.
